document.title: Home Vault High-Level Features, Requirements and BDD Acceptance Specification

source.file: Client workshop transcript supplied for requirements analysis

executiveSummary: Home Vault is a proposed mobile-first web service that gives New Zealand homeowners, renovators and small property investors one visual, structured place to retain the information, documents, reminders, tasks, assets and costs associated with each property. The initial proposition replaces fragmented spreadsheets, email, calendar entries, paper receipts, informal contact names and physical reminders such as retained paint cans. A free one-property record is intended to build reach, while a paid plan adds active property, maintenance, renovation, financial and reporting tools. The longer-term opportunity is a buyer-safe property passport and ownership transfer experience that preserves useful property knowledge without disclosing a seller's confidential renovation economics.

customerSegments.name: Small-portfolio residential property investors
customerSegments.definition: New Zealand owners with more than one property, typically two to nine properties, who manage property knowledge themselves rather than using specialist portfolio software.
needs: A reliable record for each property and room
Asset, invoice, expense and renovation-cost visibility
Information and exports suitable for accountants

customerSegments.name: Renovators and property flippers
customerSegments.definition: People actively improving and reselling property who need room-level photos, tasks, budgets, costs, assets and before-and-after records.
needs: A future buyer-safe handover that protects margin and cost details

customerSegments.name: Owner-occupiers
customerSegments.definition: Single-property homeowners who need a simple home information record and may later renovate, acquire another property or upgrade to active management tools.
needs: One place for paint colours, photos and property documents
A path to paid reminders, assets and reporting when needs grow

customerSegments.name: Property collaborators
customerSegments.definition: Partners, family members and other trusted people invited by an owner to help view or manage property information.
needs: Controlled access to sensitive financial records

customerSegments.name: Property buyers, sellers and agents
customerSegments.definition: Participants in a property sale who may use a paid property passport and ownership-claim process.
needs: Useful room, asset and warranty information
Protection of the seller's confidential renovation and purchase economics

currentAlternatives: Physical reminders such as retained paint cans and paper receipts
Specialist property-management software used by larger portfolios
marketPosition.positioning: Home Vault sits between unstructured personal tools and professional property-management platforms. It is intended to be easier and more valuable than a spreadsheet for self-managing owners, without requiring the complexity of enterprise or agency property-management software.
differentiators: Documents, tasks, reminders and financial records in one place
Future privacy-aware property passport and transfer
marketPosition.experienceReference: A familiar modern New Zealand property-platform experience, with Homes.co.nz used only as a usability reference. No third-party branding or protected visual design is to be copied.

problemsToSolve.problem: Property information is fragmented across memory, paper, email, texts, documents, spreadsheets and calendars.
problemsToSolve.impact: Owners waste time searching and cannot rely on a complete record.

problemsToSolve.problem: Owners lose practical knowledge such as paint colours, product details and which trade completed work.
problemsToSolve.impact: Maintenance and repeat work are slower, less accurate and more expensive.

problemsToSolve.problem: Warranties, servicing dates and recurring maintenance are easy to miss.
problemsToSolve.impact: Owners may lose warranty value, defer maintenance or incur avoidable costs.

problemsToSolve.problem: Asset, invoice and depreciation information is difficult to assemble for accountants.
problemsToSolve.impact: Financial reporting is incomplete and owners may miss legitimate depreciation information.

problemsToSolve.problem: Renovation costs and ongoing property expenses are maintained in separate spreadsheets or not tracked consistently.
problemsToSolve.impact: Owners cannot easily understand spend by property, room, category or period.

problemsToSolve.problem: Existing tools are either too manual or designed for larger professional property operations.
problemsToSolve.impact: Small-portfolio owners lack a right-sized product that is worth paying for.

problemsToSolve.problem: Useful knowledge is lost when a property is sold, while sellers do not want to disclose confidential renovation economics.
problemsToSolve.impact: Buyers receive an incomplete handover and sellers face privacy and commercial concerns.

problemsToSolve.problem: Property records are often text-heavy and administrative rather than visual and engaging.
problemsToSolve.impact: Owners are less likely to keep records current or celebrate and share renovation progress.

desiredOutcomes: Create one trusted source of property knowledge for each owner.
Reduce the time and effort needed to find property, room, asset, trade and document information.
Protect value by keeping warranties, service dates and recurring maintenance visible.
Make renovation and ownership costs understandable by property, room, category and period.
Make accountant handover and asset/depreciation preparation easier.
Provide an image-rich experience that encourages regular use and supports before-and-after storytelling.
Build a large free-user base with a credible path to paid subscriptions and a future strategic property-platform partnership or acquisition.
productPrinciples: The product must provide clearer value and be easier to use than a spreadsheet.
The information hierarchy must remain intuitive: portfolio, property, room, asset or record.
Capturing a photo or document should be fast on a mobile browser.
The free experience must be genuinely useful for one property; paid value must come from active management, automation and reporting.
The design must be visual, modern and mobile-first while remaining a responsive web service for the initial release.
Customer behaviour will inform later changes; the scope is expected to adapt after real-world validation.
Private financial information must not be exposed through collaboration or future ownership transfer.

actors.name: Visitor
actors.description: A prospective customer viewing the public website.

actors.name: Free owner
actors.description: A registered customer maintaining one property's core information.

actors.name: Paid owner or portfolio administrator
actors.description: A subscriber managing active property, asset, task, cost and reporting features.

actors.name: Invited administrator
actors.description: A trusted user allowed to manage the owner's permitted property information.

actors.name: Read-only collaborator
actors.description: A trusted user allowed to view but not change permitted property information.

actors.name: Future buyer or new owner
actors.description: A recipient of a buyer-safe property passport who may claim transferred property information.

userFlows.name: Discover, register and start
userFlows.trigger: A visitor wants a better way to retain home or property information.
steps: View the public proposition and compare the free and paid value.
Create an account or sign in.
Complete a basic profile.
Start the guided add-property flow.
userFlows.outcome: The customer reaches a usable first-property record with minimal friction.

userFlows.name: Add a property and its rooms
userFlows.trigger: A registered owner wants to establish a property record.
steps: Enter or look up the property address.
Confirm available property details or enter them manually.
Classify the property, including whether it is the owner's home or a rental/investment property.
Accept suggested standard rooms and add, rename or remove rooms.
userFlows.outcome: A structured property-and-room record is ready for content.

userFlows.name: Build the visual room record
userFlows.trigger: An owner wants to remember what is in a room and how it has changed.
steps: Open a room within a property.
Upload current or before-and-after photos.
Record paint colours, finishes and room notes.
Add related assets, documents, costs or tasks where the owner's plan permits.
userFlows.outcome: The room becomes a useful, visual source of truth.

userFlows.name: Record an asset, invoice and warranty
userFlows.trigger: An appliance, fixture or other depreciable/maintainable item is purchased or identified.
steps: Select the property and, where relevant, the room.
Create the asset with purchase, supplier/trade and product details.
Upload the invoice, receipt and warranty documents.
Record warranty expiry and service information.
userFlows.outcome: The asset and its supporting evidence can be found, maintained and reported.

userFlows.name: Plan and complete property work
userFlows.trigger: Maintenance or renovation work needs to be planned or repeated.
steps: Create a task against a property, room or asset.
Set a due date and optional recurrence.
Review tasks in calendar or Kanban-style views.
Receive an email reminder and complete or reschedule the task.
userFlows.outcome: Important work is visible and less likely to be missed.

userFlows.name: Track costs, expenses and renovation budget
userFlows.trigger: The owner receives a bill, incurs a renovation cost or wants to understand household operating costs.
steps: Choose asset, renovation cost or ongoing expense.
Assign the record to a property and optionally a room.
Categorise the record, including electricity, gas, rates, cleaning or maintenance.
Upload the bill or invoice and review totals by period, category, property or room.
userFlows.outcome: The owner can understand property cost and budget performance, including a twelve-month utility view.

userFlows.name: Review and export property information
userFlows.trigger: The owner needs a consolidated view or information for an accountant.
steps: Select portfolio, property or room scope.
Review assets, tasks, costs, expenses, photos and relevant documents.
Generate a Property Information Report or accountant-focused export.
Download or share the permitted output.
userFlows.outcome: Useful property knowledge is available without rebuilding a spreadsheet.

userFlows.name: Invite and collaborate
userFlows.trigger: An owner wants a partner or trusted person to help manage or view information.
steps: Invite the person by email.
Assign administrator or read-only access.
The invitee accepts and accesses only permitted information.
Authorised users add or review comments at property or room level.
userFlows.outcome: Property knowledge can be shared without surrendering control.

userFlows.name: Upgrade for active management
userFlows.trigger: A free owner needs another property or a paid feature.
steps: Select a paid feature or attempt to add another property.
Review paid-plan value and the current monthly/annual price.
Complete subscription checkout.
Return to the original action with paid access enabled.
userFlows.outcome: The customer converts without losing existing property information.

userFlows.name: Create a buyer-safe passport and transfer ownership
userFlows.trigger: A recorded property is being sold.
steps: The seller generates a buyer-safe Property Passport.
The seller reviews the included rooms, assets and warranty information.
The service excludes confidential renovation labour, material costs and seller-only financial records.
Following sale, the new owner claims the property and receives the approved transferable record.
userFlows.outcome: Useful property knowledge survives a sale without exposing the seller's confidential economics.

features.name: Public website, account access and profile
features.summary: Explain the proposition, convert visitors to a free account and provide secure access to a personal profile.

requirements.statement: The public website shall explain the one-place property record proposition, the free one-property offer and the additional value of the paid plan, with a clear registration call to action.

bddTests.title: Visitor understands the proposition and starts registration
given: A visitor is not signed in
The visitor is on the public website
when: The visitor reviews the offer
The visitor selects the free-account call to action
then: The free one-property entitlement is visible
Paid-plan value is distinguishable
The registration flow opens

requirements.statement: The service shall support account registration, sign-in, sign-out and password recovery using an email address.

bddTests.title: Registered customer recovers account access
given: A registered customer cannot remember the password
when: The customer requests password recovery
The customer completes the emailed recovery process
then: The customer can set a new password
The customer can sign in without losing property data

requirements.statement: A registered customer shall be able to maintain a personal profile, including display name and profile photo.

bddTests.title: Customer updates profile details
given: A customer is signed in
when: The customer updates the display name and profile photo
The customer saves the profile
then: The saved profile is shown on the next visit
The updated identity is used in collaborative views

features.name: Plans, subscription and access
features.summary: Provide a genuinely useful free record and a clear paid path for active property management.

requirements.statement: The free plan shall allow one property and its rooms to retain core information, photos, paint details and documents.

bddTests.title: Free customer builds one useful property record
given: A free customer has no property
when: The customer adds one property
The customer adds rooms, photos, paint details and documents
then: The information is saved
The customer can return to and view the property record
No paid subscription is required for the core record

requirements.statement: The paid plan shall unlock additional properties and active tools including assets, automated or recurring tasks, reminders, calendars, financial tracking and reporting.

bddTests.title: Paid customer receives active management tools
given: A free customer has an existing property record
when: The customer completes a paid subscription
then: The existing record is preserved
Paid features become available
The customer can add another property

requirements.statement: The launch checkout shall support the approved pricing options; the workshop hypothesis is NZD 19 per month or NZD 199 per year, subject to client and market validation.

bddTests.title: Customer chooses an approved billing period
given: Monthly and annual prices have been approved and configured
when: A customer chooses a billing period and completes checkout
then: The selected price and renewal period are confirmed before payment
The subscription reflects the selected billing period

features.name: Property portfolio and setup
features.access: Free for one property; paid for multiple properties
features.summary: Create and manage structured property records without requiring specialist property-management knowledge.

requirements.statement: A customer shall be able to add, view, edit and archive a property record, subject to the customer's plan limit.

bddTests.title: Customer adds a property within the plan limit
given: A signed-in customer is below the plan's property limit
when: The customer enters the required property details and saves
then: The property appears in the portfolio
The customer can reopen and edit it

requirements.statement: The property setup shall capture the address and owner-selected property context, including whether the property is the customer's home or a rental/investment property.

bddTests.title: Customer classifies a new property
given: A customer is adding a property
when: The customer enters an address and selects the property context
then: The classification is stored
The property displays the selected context

requirements.statement: Where a lawful and commercially available property-data source is approved, the setup shall pre-populate available property information and allow the customer to confirm or correct it; manual entry shall always remain available.

bddTests.title: Property lookup fails without blocking setup
given: A customer enters an address
No approved lookup result is available
when: The customer continues with setup
then: Manual entry is offered
The property can be completed without external data

requirements.statement: New properties shall offer a practical default set of rooms, and authorised customers shall be able to add, rename, reorder and remove rooms.

bddTests.title: Customer tailors the room list
given: A property has been created with suggested rooms
when: The customer adds a custom room and renames an existing room
then: The revised room list is saved
Room-specific records use the revised names

features.name: Rooms and visual home record
features.access: All registered users within plan limits
features.summary: Make each room an engaging, image-rich record of finishes, history and related property information.

requirements.statement: An authorised customer shall be able to upload and organise multiple photos against a room.

bddTests.title: Customer uploads room photos from a mobile browser
given: An authorised customer is viewing a room on a mobile browser
when: The customer selects and uploads multiple photos
then: Upload progress and completion are clear
The photos appear in the room record
The photos remain available after the customer signs in again

requirements.statement: A room record shall support practical finish information, including wall or surface paint colour, brand or reference details and free-text notes.

bddTests.title: Customer retrieves a saved paint reference
given: A room has a saved paint colour and brand reference
when: The customer opens the room record
then: The paint information is visible with the room photos
The customer can edit the information

requirements.statement: Room photos shall be capable of being labelled or ordered to show before-and-after renovation states.

bddTests.title: Customer creates a before-and-after view
given: A room has at least one pre-renovation and one post-renovation photo
when: The customer labels the photos as before and after
then: The room presents the images as a clear comparison

requirements.statement: A customer should be able to create a privacy-checked social-ready before-and-after image or link without exposing private property or financial information.

bddTests.title: Social share excludes private information
given: A room has a before-and-after comparison
The property also contains private financial records
when: The customer creates a social-ready share
then: Only the selected images and approved caption are included
No address or financial information is included unless explicitly selected

features.name: Assets, invoices, warranties and trade records
features.summary: Retain the evidence and dates needed to own, maintain and report on items within a property.

requirements.statement: An authorised paid user shall be able to create an asset at property or room level with description, product details, purchase date and optional supplier or trade contact.

bddTests.title: Customer records a room asset
given: A paid customer is viewing a room
when: The customer records an appliance and purchase details
then: The asset appears in both the room and property asset views
The saved details can be edited

requirements.statement: An asset shall support attached invoices, receipts, warranty documents and relevant photos.

bddTests.title: Customer finds an asset warranty document
given: An asset has an attached warranty document
when: The customer opens the asset
then: The document name and type are visible
The authorised customer can view or download it

requirements.statement: An asset shall support warranty expiry, recommended service date and service history information that can create related reminders or tasks.

bddTests.title: Warranty date creates a reminder
given: An asset has a future warranty expiry
The customer has reminder access
when: The customer enables a pre-expiry reminder
then: A dated reminder is created against the asset
The reminder appears in the property calendar

requirements.statement: The service shall maintain an asset register with purchase-value and depreciation-input fields suitable for review or export to an accountant; the service shall not present itself as tax advice.

bddTests.title: Customer prepares asset information for an accountant
given: A property contains assets with purchase details
when: The customer requests the accountant asset export
then: The export includes the recorded asset and purchase fields
The output clearly indicates that accounting treatment requires professional confirmation

features.name: Tasks, reminders and calendar
features.summary: Make maintenance and renovation work visible, repeatable and less likely to be missed.

requirements.statement: An authorised paid user shall be able to create a dated task against a property, room or asset and assign notes and status.

bddTests.title: Customer creates a room maintenance task
given: A paid customer is viewing a room
when: The customer adds a dated maintenance task
then: The task is linked to the room and property
The task appears in open-task views

requirements.statement: A task or reminder shall support recurrence, including monthly and annual patterns, and shall create the next occurrence without duplicating completed history.

bddTests.title: Recurring task advances after completion
given: A monthly cleaning task is due
when: The customer marks the occurrence complete
then: The completed occurrence remains in history
The next occurrence is scheduled one month later

requirements.statement: Paid customers shall be able to review work in calendar and Kanban-style task views, with filters for portfolio, property, room, asset, status and date.

bddTests.title: Customer filters work to one property
given: A paid customer has tasks across multiple properties
when: The customer filters the calendar to one property
then: Only tasks for that property are shown
The same task records remain available in the Kanban view

requirements.statement: The service shall send scheduled email reminders for enabled due dates, including examples such as heat-pump servicing, filter or UV-lamp replacement and smoke-alarm testing.

bddTests.title: Customer receives a due-date email reminder
given: A reminder is enabled
The configured notification time has arrived
when: The scheduled reminder process runs
then: An email is sent to the authorised recipient
The email identifies the property, item and due action
The send outcome is recorded

features.name: Costs, expenses and renovation budgets
features.summary: Provide a consistent financial record for assets, renovations and ongoing property ownership.

requirements.statement: The service shall distinguish asset purchases, renovation costs and ongoing property expenses as separate financial record types.

bddTests.title: Customer records different financial types
given: A paid customer is adding a financial record
when: The customer selects asset purchase, renovation cost or ongoing expense
then: Fields and reporting classification match the selected type
The record is not double-counted across types

requirements.statement: A financial record shall be assignable to a property and, where relevant, a room, with amount, date, category, notes and supporting bill, receipt or invoice.

bddTests.title: Customer uploads a room renovation invoice
given: A paid customer is viewing a room
when: The customer enters a renovation cost and uploads its invoice
then: The cost appears in room and property totals
The invoice is accessible to authorised users

requirements.statement: Ongoing expense categories shall include, at minimum, electricity, gas, rates, cleaning and maintenance, with customer-defined categories available where required.

bddTests.title: Customer categorises a utility bill
given: A paid customer has an electricity bill
when: The customer records the amount and selects electricity
then: The expense is included in electricity totals
The uploaded bill remains linked to the record

requirements.statement: The service shall support renovation budgets and actual-cost comparison, plus period views that can show at least twelve months of household operating expenses by property and category.

bddTests.title: Customer reviews twelve months of electricity cost
given: A property has twelve months of electricity expenses
when: The customer selects the property, electricity category and twelve-month period
then: The service shows the total and period breakdown
The figures reconcile to the underlying expense records

features.name: Property reporting and exports
features.summary: Turn the retained information into useful owner, renovation and accountant views.

requirements.statement: Paid customers shall be able to review assets, tasks, costs, expenses and relevant documents at portfolio, property and room scope.

bddTests.title: Customer moves from property to room reporting
given: A property contains records across multiple rooms
when: The customer changes report scope from property to one room
then: Totals and lists update to the selected room
The property-level source records remain unchanged

requirements.statement: The service shall generate a client-approved Property Information Report containing the selected property's room photos, finish information, assets, warranties, maintenance and permitted supporting records.

bddTests.title: Customer generates a property information report
given: A paid customer's property contains room and asset information
when: The customer selects the report sections and generates the report
then: The output contains only the selected and permitted information
The report identifies the property and generation date

requirements.statement: The service shall provide downloadable accountant-focused exports for asset/depreciation inputs and property or room spend, with clear date and category fields.

bddTests.title: Accountant export reconciles to recorded spend
given: A property has dated assets, renovation costs and expenses
when: The customer exports the selected financial period
then: Each exported row identifies its record type and source scope
Exported totals reconcile to the in-service report

features.name: Users, permissions and collaboration
features.summary: Allow trusted people to participate without weakening the owner's control or confidentiality.

requirements.statement: A paid owner shall be able to invite another user and assign administrator or read-only access.

bddTests.title: Owner invites a read-only collaborator
given: A paid owner has a property
when: The owner invites a user with read-only access
The invitee accepts
then: The invitee can view permitted information
The invitee cannot create, edit or delete records

requirements.statement: Only an owner or authorised administrator shall be able to change shared property information, and only the owner shall be able to manage ownership, subscription and transfer settings.

bddTests.title: Administrator cannot transfer ownership
given: An invited administrator is signed in
when: The administrator opens property settings
then: The administrator can manage permitted content
Ownership, subscription and transfer controls are unavailable

requirements.statement: Authorised users shall be able to add and review timestamped comments or notes at property and room level.

bddTests.title: Collaborator adds a room comment
given: An authorised administrator is viewing a room
when: The administrator adds a comment
then: The comment shows its author and time
Permitted users can view the comment in the room record

features.name: Preferences and display
features.summary: Give each customer a comfortable and consistent personal experience.

requirements.statement: A registered customer shall be able to select light or dark display mode, and the preference shall persist across sessions on supported devices.

bddTests.title: Display preference persists
given: A signed-in customer selects dark mode
when: The customer signs out and later signs in again
then: The service opens using dark mode
All primary workflows remain readable and usable

requirements.statement: A customer shall be able to manage email-reminder preferences without deleting the underlying tasks or dates.

bddTests.title: Customer pauses reminder emails but retains tasks
given: A customer has scheduled tasks and email reminders
when: The customer disables email reminders
then: No new reminder emails are sent while disabled
The tasks and due dates remain visible in the service

features.name: Property Passport and ownership transfer
features.access: Future paid add-on or approved entitlement
features.summary: Support a sale-time information product and controlled handover to the new owner.

requirements.statement: A seller shall be able to generate a separately chargeable buyer-safe Property Passport for an eligible property.

bddTests.title: Seller creates a passport preview
given: A property has sufficient room and asset information
The seller has the required entitlement
when: The seller creates a Property Passport preview
then: The preview lists included information
The seller can review it before sharing or transfer

requirements.statement: The transferable record shall include approved room, asset, warranty and maintenance information but exclude seller-only renovation labour, material costs, margin and other confidential financial records.

bddTests.title: Buyer-safe output protects seller economics
given: A property contains assets, warranty documents and confidential renovation costs
when: The seller generates the buyer-safe passport
then: Approved asset and warranty information is included
Renovation labour, material cost and seller margin information is excluded

requirements.statement: Following an authorised property sale, the seller shall be able to initiate transfer and the new owner shall be able to claim the approved transferable record.

bddTests.title: New owner claims a transferred property
given: The seller has initiated transfer to the buyer's verified account
when: The buyer accepts and claims the property
then: The buyer becomes the owner of the transferable record
The former owner loses ongoing management access unless separately invited
Seller-only records remain private and retained according to policy

requirements.statement: The service shall present the seller with an explicit inclusion and exclusion summary before any passport is shared or ownership is transferred.

bddTests.title: Transfer requires informed confirmation
given: A seller has prepared a transfer
when: The seller reaches final confirmation
then: Included and excluded information is summarised
The transfer cannot proceed without explicit confirmation

features.name: Smart capture and proactive guidance
features.summary: Reduce manual data entry and help owners identify useful maintenance or improvement actions.

requirements.statement: The service may support barcode or QR-code capture to look up product details from an approved data source, while allowing customer correction and manual entry.

bddTests.title: Barcode lookup remains editable
given: A customer is adding an asset
An approved product lookup source is available
when: The customer scans a supported barcode
then: Matched product details are proposed
The customer can correct the details before saving
Manual entry remains available if no match is found

requirements.statement: The service may analyse an uploaded image to propose metadata such as a paint colour or product reference, subject to customer confirmation.

bddTests.title: Image analysis never silently overwrites customer data
given: A customer uploads a room or product image
when: The service proposes detected metadata
then: The proposal is labelled as an estimate
No metadata is saved until the customer confirms or edits it

requirements.statement: The service may provide configurable maintenance prompts for common property needs, including heat-pump servicing, filter and UV-lamp replacement, smoke-alarm testing, annual checks and relevant council changes.

bddTests.title: Customer controls a suggested maintenance task
given: The service identifies a relevant maintenance suggestion
when: The suggestion is shown to the customer
then: The reason and proposed timing are clear
The customer can accept, edit or dismiss it
A task is created only after acceptance

requirements.statement: The service may offer contextual improvement insights and approved supplier referrals, such as a solar opportunity based on recorded energy costs, with commercial relationships disclosed.

bddTests.title: Commercial referral is transparent
given: A customer is eligible for a contextual supplier suggestion
when: The suggestion is displayed
then: Any commercial relationship is disclosed
The customer can dismiss the suggestion
No contact details are shared without consent

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: Before public launch, the service shall have client-approved terms of use and privacy information that accurately describes data collection, use, storage, sharing and customer choices, supported by appropriate New Zealand legal review.
Property, document and financial information shall be accessible only to authenticated and authorised users, with role and ownership rules enforced on the server side.

The release process shall include security, penetration and data-access testing proportionate to the sensitivity and nationwide ambition of the service, with critical findings resolved before public launch.
All MVP workflows shall operate in supported modern mobile and desktop browsers; a native mobile application is not required for the initial release.
The experience shall use clear language, visible status and accessible interaction patterns so customers can complete core flows without specialist property or accounting knowledge.
Uploads shall show status, reject unsupported or unsafe files clearly, preserve authorised access and prevent an apparent success when storage fails.
Scheduled reminder processing shall be observable and retryable, with send outcomes recorded so the service can identify failures without creating duplicate notices.

The architecture shall support progressive growth from early customers to nationwide use without redesigning the core property-room-asset model; measurable performance targets shall be agreed before build completion.
Reports and exports shall reconcile to source records, retain their scope and date context and apply permission and transfer-exclusion rules consistently.
Automated or AI-assisted suggestions shall be distinguishable from customer-confirmed facts and shall not silently change property records or share customer information.

commercialModel.freePlan: One property with core information, rooms, photos, paint/finish details and documents.
commercialModel.paidPlan: Multiple properties plus active asset, task, reminder, calendar, expense, cost, budget and reporting tools.

pricingHypothesis.status: Workshop hypothesis requiring approval and market validation

commercialModel.sustainabilityObjective: Subscription revenue should first cover platform, support and marketing costs and then support a sustainable owner-operated business.
commercialModel.growthObjective: Use a genuinely valuable free plan to build adoption, learn from customer behaviour and create an ethical path to paid conversion when customers need active management tools.

style: Clear property, room and record navigation
Optional light and dark display modes
referenceBoundaries: Homes.co.nz is a familiarity and usability reference only.
Instagram-like visual engagement may inform photo interactions, but the product must retain its own identity and privacy controls.
No third-party brand, interface or protected design is to be copied.
clientInputs: Public website tone and approved copy
Instagram, Facebook and X/Twitter handle decisions

solutionAssumptions: The initial product is one responsive web application; there is no native mobile application in the initial scope.
The experience will be image-rich and optimised for frequent mobile-browser capture.

The workshop proposed Next.js for the web application and server-side functions, Supabase for the database and document storage, scheduled jobs for reminders and SendGrid for initial email delivery; final technology choices remain subject to technical validation.
Homes.co.nz is an experience-category reference only and does not grant access to its data, branding, layouts or interfaces.
Any third-party property or product lookup requires a lawful, approved and commercially viable data source.
The final product name, logo, domain, colour palette and social handles remain client decisions.
Delivery timing will be agreed after requirements approval and MVP sizing.
initialScope: Public website, registration, authentication and profile
Room photos, paint/finish records and documents
Assets, invoices, warranties and service information
Tasks, recurring reminders, email notifications, calendar and Kanban views
Renovation costs, ongoing expenses, categories, budgets and twelve-month views
Terms, privacy, access control and pre-launch security assurance
postMvpScope: Further reporting refinements based on customer behaviour
futureScope: AI-assisted paint, image and product metadata
Energy and solar insights with transparent supplier referrals
outOfInitialScope: Automated legal, tax, depreciation or accounting advice
